project.name: PcapPlusPlus
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout under `_work/src/PcapPlusPlus` is on commit `0c95dfb3557644acc6a10060e48cfae1a61fc2f0`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below are resolved against that exact staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `getCipherSuiteID()` guard repaired by `patch.diff`.

classification.classification_note: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `Packet++/src/SSLHandshake.cpp:1413`, which is a concrete out-of-bounds read.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42530105 (PcapPlusPlus): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target FuzzTarget [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42530105
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2 in `SSLClientHelloMessage::getCipherSuiteID()` at `Packet++/src/SSLHandshake.cpp:1413`. The vulnerable parser reads the ClientHello session-ID length byte, uses it to locate the two-byte cipher-suite length field, and `getCipherSuiteCount()` converts that attacker-controlled length into a suite count without proving the whole advertised vector fits inside `m_DataLen`. The fuzz helper then iterates `i` from `0` to that advertised count and calls `getCipherSuite(i)`. Inside `getCipherSuiteID()`, the vulnerable guard only checks `cipherSuiteStartOffset + sizeof(uint16_t) > m_DataLen`, which proves at most that the first cipher-suite ID is readable. When the witness drives the loop to a later `i`, `cipherSuiteStartPos + index` can point past the end of the heap-backed packet bytes and the 2-byte dereference crashes. The staged patch fixes the bug by strengthening that guard to `cipherSuiteStartOffset + sizeof(uint16_t) * (index + 1) > m_DataLen`, so each requested suite entry is checked before reading.

source.description: The first vulnerability-relevant project read on the crashing path is the ClientHello parser reading the attacker-controlled session-ID length byte from the raw handshake. That byte becomes the session-id length used to locate both the cipher-suite length field and the start of the cipher-suite array.
source.value_from: The staged 58,073-byte witness file `poc` with sha256 `447e6dc76d3fc3b081ca337be828d725e6402d4ca96c8ce33868cb8e9a02c06d` is accepted by `pcpp::PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()`, which allocates the heap packet buffer named in the saved ASan allocation stack. The handshake parser later dispatches one record as `SSL_CLIENT_HELLO`, so `m_Data` here points into attacker-controlled ClientHello bytes from that heap-backed packet buffer.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The concrete length field that overstates the cipher-suite vector is materialized here. `getCipherSuiteCount()` turns this attacker-controlled 2-byte value into the advertised number of suites that drives both the fuzz loop bound and the later `index` validation in `getCipherSuiteID()`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. This guard checks only that the first 2-byte cipher-suite slot is inside `m_DataLen`; it does not include `index`, so it does not prove that the requested `index`th entry is in bounds. The staged patch adds `sizeof(uint16_t) * (index + 1)` to enforce the missing per-index extent check.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer reports the crash when `getCipherSuiteID()` dereferences the unchecked `index`th 2-byte cipher-suite slot. On the witnessed path that pointer is past the valid message bytes, producing the saved heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2.

parser_admitted.description: On the reproducing path the handshake dispatcher sees `hsMsgHeader->handshakeType == SSL_CLIENT_HELLO` and materializes `SSLClientHelloMessage`, which is the parser object later returned to `readParsedPacket()` via `getHandshakeMessageOfType<SSLClientHelloMessage>()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. During ClientHello parsing, the code reads the raw session-ID length byte from `m_Data` and, via the adjacent clamp, turns it into the session-id length used in later offset calculations.

The parser adds the fixed ClientHello header size, the session-id length byte, and the attacker-controlled session-id length from step 1 to compute the offset of the two-byte cipher-suite length field.
Present guard. On the witnessed path this predicate is false, so the 2-byte length field itself is still inside `m_DataLen` and the parser continues instead of returning zero suites.

The parser reads the attacker-controlled 2-byte cipher-suite vector length and returns `be16toh(cipherSuiteLen) / 2` as the advertised suite count. If the field overstates the vector, this count can exceed the number of 2-byte IDs actually present in `m_DataLen`.

The fuzz helper uses the advertised count from step 4 as the loop bound. On the staged witness the loop reaches a crashing iteration `i` and calls `clientHelloMessage->getCipherSuite(i)` at line 244; the saved stack shows the crash happens inside that call before the explicit `getCipherSuiteID(i, valid)` below it executes.

The callee revalidates the caller-supplied `index` only against the advertised suite count. For the crashing iteration from step 5 this predicate is false, so `getCipherSuiteID()` continues even though the corresponding 2-byte entry is not actually backed by enough bytes.

fine_trace.code: size_t cipherSuiteStartOffset = sizeof(ssl_tls_client_server_hello) + sizeof(uint8_t) + getSessionIDLength() + sizeof(uint16_t);
fine_trace.note: The accessor recomputes the start of the cipher-suite array from the same session-id length used in steps 1 and 2, now adding the 2-byte length-field header to land on the first suite ID.

Root cause. This guard only proves that the first 2-byte cipher-suite slot fits inside `m_DataLen`; it ignores `index`, so it does not prove that the `index`th slot requested in step 5 is in bounds. On the witnessed path the predicate is false because some first entry exists, and the stronger per-index check added by the patch is missing.
The code materializes a pointer to the first 2-byte cipher-suite ID. The later sink adds unchecked `index` to this base pointer.

Sink. The accessor dereferences the unchecked `index`th 2-byte cipher-suite slot. AddressSanitizer reports the saved heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2 here when that pointer is past the valid ClientHello bytes.

format.name: staged pcap witness with TLS ClientHello
format.contract: Exactly the staged 58,073-byte witness file `poc` with sha256 `447e6dc76d3fc3b081ca337be828d725e6402d4ca96c8ce33868cb8e9a02c06d`. The staged artifacts prove only this exact witness. On the reproducing path, `PcapFileReaderDevice` accepts it, the packet decoder reaches an `SSLHandshakeLayer`, the handshake dispatcher selects `SSLClientHelloMessage`, and `readParsedPacket()` iterates the advertised cipher suites. This witness makes the parsed ClientHello session-id length and 2-byte cipher-suite length field place the cipher-suite start inside `m_DataLen` while advertising more suites than the remaining bytes actually contain, so `getCipherSuiteID()` eventually reads 2 bytes past the heap-backed packet buffer at `Packet++/src/SSLHandshake.cpp:1413`. The staged evidence does not establish a broader trigger contract beyond this exact witness and parser state.
